Colorado Time Systems (CTS) is an American manufacturer of aquatic timing,
scoring, and display systems, based in Loveland, Colorado. Founded in 1972 by
engineers from Hewlett-Packard, it is one of the principal suppliers of swimming,
diving, and water polo timing equipment, particularly in the United States, and
since the early 2010s has been part of the recreation company PlayCore.[^wiki-cts][^about]

Much of the named hardware documented in the
[equipment reference](../equipment/index.md) is made by CTS.

## History

CTS traces its origins to the Test & Measurement division of Hewlett-Packard
(HP). HP was exploring the sports-timing market and chose aquatics because it
demanded especially precise measurement; in 1972 a group of four HP engineers left
to found the company.[^wiki-cts][^about][^campusrec]

CTS's co-founder William "Bill" Beierwaltes had worked at Hewlett-Packard from 1964
to 1974 as a product manager for its electronic measuring equipment. In 1985 he
started Colorado Memory Systems as a division of CTS to sell computer data-storage
products; that business became independent in May 1990 and was acquired by
Hewlett-Packard in September 1992.[^wiki-cts][^cms]

CTS was later acquired by PlayCore, a Chattanooga, Tennessee recreation company,
and became part of its EverActive Brands group. Sources give slightly different
dates: several industry and trade reports place the deal in 2012 (reported that
July, and effective around October), while Wikipedia dates it to July 2011.[^wiki-cts][^aquaticsintl][^pehub]
Manufacturing remained at the Colorado facility and general manager Anita Sayed
continued to run day-to-day operations; PlayCore was itself owned at the time by the
private-equity firm Irving Place Capital.[^aquaticsintl][^pehub]

## Products

CTS designs, manufactures, sells, and services timing, scoring, and display
equipment, with a core focus on aquatics.[^about]

- Aquatic timing, timing consoles (the current line is the Gen7
  platform), AquaGrip touchpads (which use a patented non-skid surface), start
  systems, and dedicated water-polo and diving scoring systems.[^about][^products]
- Scoreboards & displays, aquatic and multisport scoreboards and LED video
  displays.[^about][^campusrec]
- Other sports, beyond aquatics, CTS also supplies scoreboards and timing for
  sports such as basketball, football, and track.[^about]
- Software, CTS AquaSync overlays official timing and scoring data onto a live
  video stream in real time for swimming, diving, and water polo. It works with the
  Gen7 and System 6 platforms and outputs graphics over NDI to streaming software
  such as OBS and vMix, without additional timing hardware; CTS says it carries no
  subscription or annual fee.[^aquasync][^aquasync-sw]

Individual CTS products are catalogued in the
[equipment reference](../equipment/index.md): the
[Gen7 timers](../equipment/swimming/timers/index.md), the connect-hub
[Serial](../equipment/swimming/timers/gen7-serial.md) and multi-pin
[Legacy](../equipment/swimming/timers/gen7-legacy.md) consoles and the earlier
[System 6](../equipment/swimming/timers/system-6.md) and
[System 5](../equipment/swimming/timers/system-5.md) they replaced, and the
[start systems](../equipment/swimming/starter/index.md), the portable
[Infinity](../equipment/swimming/starter/infinity-start-system.md) and
[Infinity Pro](../equipment/swimming/starter/infinity-pro-start-system.md), and
the deck-wired
[Championship](../equipment/swimming/starter/championship-start-system.md) and
[Championship Elite](../equipment/swimming/starter/championship-elite-start-system.md),
which replaced the earlier deck-wired
[CHAMP-SSM](../equipment/swimming/starter/champ-ssm.md) and the 1990s loudspeaker
[SS2](../equipment/swimming/starter/ss2.md) starts, and the
[AquaGrip touchpads](../equipment/swimming/touchpad/aquagrip.md) that sense
each lane's finish, the
[backup pushbutton](../equipment/swimming/semi-automatic/pushbutton/cts.md) that backs it up, the
[RJP relay judging platforms](../equipment/swimming/relay-judging/cts.md) that
judge relay exchanges from the blocks, the
[backstroke start device](../equipment/swimming/backstroke-start/cts.md) that gives
backstrokers a fixed foothold at the start, and the
[lane speakers](../equipment/swimming/external-speaker/cts.md) the start systems drive
under each block.
Scoreboard models are added as those pages are written.

## In swim timing

The first electronic swim-timing system using in-lane touchpads is generally
credited to the Swiss company Omega, in 1967, though the 1964 Tokyo Olympic Games had
already adopted a touch board as the official timer for swimming.[^tokyo64] CTS is one of a small number of
major aquatic-timing manufacturers, alongside [Swiss Timing](swiss-timing.md) (Omega),
[Daktronics](daktronics.md), and [Seiko](seiko.md).[^wiki-timing] The company describes itself as having pioneered the first fully
automatic swim-timing system and has been a long-standing developer of touchpad
technology in the United States.[^blog]

## In competition

CTS equipment is widely used in United States collegiate and club swimming and at
national and international competitions, including NCAA championships and US Olympic
Team Trials.[^about][^campusrec] The company has been an official timing, scoring, or
display partner to organizations including USA Water Polo, US artistic
(synchronized) swimming, the Mexican Swimming Federation, the American Swimming
Coaches Association, and the China Swimming Association, and says it serves customers
in roughly 120 countries.[^wiki-cts][^aquaticsintl]

## Recognition

CTS's touchpad technology has been featured on the History Channel program *Modern
Marvels* (2008) and in a sports-invention exhibit associated with the
Smithsonian.[^wiki-cts][^blog]
